findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so bucket/object ACLs or policies could expose report data publicly.
No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket containing report and vendor data is not recorded, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted (combined with force_destroy = true) with no recovery or tamper evidence.
The ledger export bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted by default at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so reads and writes of ledger data are not auditable.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be permanently deleted or overwritten without recovery or tamper evidence.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies for this bucket, leaving it exposed to accidental public grants.
The model artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so proprietary model data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No public access block is attached, so bucket policies or ACLs could make model artifacts publicly readable.
The runbooks bucket lacks server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks often contain sensitive procedures and endpoints and are stored unencrypted by default.
No logging block is defined, so access to operational runbooks is not recorded for audit purposes.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or policies.
The audit log destination bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or access to audit logs is not independently recorded.
No public access block protects the audit log bucket, meaning a misapplied ACL or policy could expose all collected access logs.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows all audit log objects to be deleted on terraform destroy, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.
This object (a vendor roster containing potentially sensitive third-party data) is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption.
